text:
jo: quick report from a user trying the node sampleapp: when OTEL env var is set and REDACT_STRICT=1 our server logs show `req_id: <missing>` and debug traces have the span id but no correlating req id. Repro in Docker and on mac.

rhea: Hmm. Are they using our request-id middleware or relying on the client to send X-Request-Id?

jo: They have request-id middleware installed, but they said the middleware was applied after the `@opentelemetry/auto-instrumentation` import in the sample.

tariq: That ordering can cause the OTEL wrapper to capture context before our middleware mutates req/res. Also note our redact middleware runs pretty early in the chain for some templates and might zero out headers when REDACT_STRICT=1. Two races: ordering + header removal.

rhea: Which log level are they running at? If debug logging is off some hooks might be skipped.

jo: They ran with LOG_LEVEL=debug and still saw missing req id in logs. However the OTEL span shows attributes: http.request_id present. So the value exists somewhere but our loghook can't read it.

tariq: So OTEL is extracting the header and storing it on the span, but our loghook depends on req.id or req.headers['x-request-id']. If the req object is wrapped we lose the property.

rhea: Quick mitigation: make loghook look for three places in order: req.id, req.headers['x-request-id'], and span attribute via OpenTelemetry API if available. That should handle wrapped requests.

jo: Pseudocode I tossed together:
```js
function findReqId(req, res) {
  if (req && req.id) return req.id;
  if (req && req.headers && req.headers['x-request-id']) return req.headers['x-request-id'];
  const span = opentelemetry.api.trace.getSpan(opentelemetry.context.active());
  if (span) return span.attributes && (span.attributes['http.request_id'] || span.attributes['x-request-id']);
  const fromRes = res && res.getHeader && res.getHeader('x-request-id');
  return fromRes || '-';
}
```

security: Important: if we pull request ids from spans or headers, we should not log raw values under REDACT_STRICT. We need a deterministic hash using a service HMAC key. Add CONFIG: HASH_REQID=true means store hashed token in logs.

tariq: Agree. Also, we should not rely on opentelemetry API being present in all envs. Wrap that access in try/catch.

rhea: For onboarding docs: update the sampleapp README to show recommended middleware ordering and mention the env vars REDACT_ALLOWLIST_HEADERS and HASH_REQID. Also add a troubleshooting note: "If you see blank req_id, run with LOG_LEVEL=debug and check span attributes."

jo: Plan:
- hotfix: extend loghook to fallback to span attr and res header (backwards compatible)
- add unit test simulating OTEL wrapping where req object is replaced after request-id runs
- add REDACT_ALLOWLIST_HEADERS default to include x-request-id and HASH_REQID opt-in
- update quickstart docs and the sampleapp template to register request-id middleware before auto-instrumentation in examples

ci-bot: jo opened PR #5012: "fix(loghook): resilient req-id resolution across OTEL wrappers + redact hashing option"  CI started.

ops-bot: note: rolling deploy of sampleapp templates at 03:00 UTC to push docs change.

security: acked approach. Please ensure HASH_REQID uses KMS-backed key for prod deployments.

rhea: i'll add a tiny e2e test that runs the sampleapp with OTEL env var and validates logs contain hashed request id.

jo: thanks folks, will follow up once CI green and docs PR merged.
